To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substance and symbolism of CEO compensation are both important and that the substance and symbolic explanations for CEO compensation are both used in the context of the adoption of new long-term incentive compensation plans.

(1) explanations for new long term incentive plans are more likely to be symbolic than substantive; (2) explanations for new plans are more likely than explanations for existing plans to emphasize substance; and (3) the use of symbolic explanations for new plans is positively associated with firm size, institutional ownership, and board independence, while the use of substantive explanations is positively associated with CEO tenure and firm performance.

(1) the explanations for CEO long-term incentive plans are more likely to reflect substance (i.e., economic and human resource logies) than symbolism (i.e., political logics), and (2) the use of economic logics in explanations for new CEO long-term incentive plan is more likely when firms are in a high-growth industry, and the use of human resource logics is more likely in firms with high CEO tenure and high CEO ownership.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how organizations explain the compensation of CEOs.
how the explanations for the adoption of new long-term incentive (LTI) plans are shaped by the structural and interest-based forces of institutional, demographic, economic, and political factors.
the process by which new compensation plans are legitimated and the factors that influence this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings in this paper suggest that the use of explanations of CEO compensation reflects both substantive and symbolic considerations.

the findings in this paper support the notion that the explanations used by companies to justify the adoption of new long-term incentive (LTI) plans are both symbolic and substantive in nature, and that these symbolic and substantive explanations are influenced by a variety of factors.
the findings support the notion of the existence of a relationship between substance and symbol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the explanations for CEO pay are not just a matter of what is said, but also what is meant.
the explanations of CEO compensation reflect the substantive and symbolic dimensions of CEO compensation.
we are trying to develop a theoretical framework that can help to explain why alternative explanations for CEO compensation are used to reduce ambiguity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the explanations used by firms to justify CEO compensation are not simply the result of a single logic, such as agency theory, but reflect a combination of logics.
CEO pay may be driven by substantive and symbolic considerations simultaneously.
CEO compensation is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by both economic and political considerations, as well as symbolic concerns.
